metadata.title: Theory of Everything Research Programme: Block V Reflective Self-Modelling Confirmatory Experiment Software and Reproducibility Package.
metadata.description:
This software release provides the executable and reproducibility infrastructure for the preregistered confirmatory study in Experimental Block V of the Theory of Everything Research Programme.

The study was preregistered at OSF under DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/JZ4ED. Before any confirmatory seed was executed, a post-registration audit identified two execution-level ambiguities. A clarification update was publicly accepted by OSF before confirmatory execution. The clarification fixed the exact H5.1 matched self-irrelevant control and fixed utility as the primary H5.6 bypass metric without changing the frozen hypotheses, seeds, held-out variants, architecture classes, misinformation/correction procedures, impairment ranges or other scientific criteria.

The package implements the frozen Block V protocol and preserves the six confirmatory manifests and integrity locks, twenty held-out seeds, confirmatory-only task variants, S0-S4 architecture classes, H_ERROR and H_EXTERNAL bypasses, self-monitor misinformation and correction/rescue interventions, unannounced internal-impairment assays, shuffled-monitor controls, world-only uncertainty controls, provenance capture, automated decision logic and independent reproduction checks.

The confirmatory decisions were RETAIN for H5.1, H5.2, H5.3 and H5.5; RESTRICT for H5.4; and REDUCE for H5.6. The results support a scoped causal role for self-related estimates in adaptive control, including impairment-sensitive recovery and misinformation/correction rescue. However, the externally supplied calibrated-confidence bypass reproduced the registered downstream control function closely enough to defeat a stronger claim that endogenous reflective self-modelling is necessary.

This release is paired with the Block V confirmatory dataset and decision record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23321507) and implements the experimental methodology described in Working Paper III (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230).

The study does not establish phenomenal consciousness, subjective experience, sentience, human-like selfhood or conscious introspection.
